body:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager — Sev2: streaming tail latency spike detected (p99 SLO breach)

samir: I’m on it. seeing alert: streaming_tail.p99 800ms -> 3.2s across prod-us-* at 15:11 UTC

maya: which surface? SSE or websockets?

samir: mostly SSE and websocket chunking. customers reporting long gaps between chunks (10-30s) and occasional connection resets

ingrid: logs show a bunch of upstream timeouts from proxy: 
```
upstream read timeout after 30s (client_id=acct-42)
[proxy] flushed 0 bytes for 18s
```

ops_jamie: was there a deploy recently?

samir: small proxy change rolled at 15:03 that adjusted output buffering / flush thresholds (agent: proxy-v2.14.7)

kt: p95 jumped too — 120ms -> 450ms. error rate for streaming endpoints up 0.6% -> 2.8%

maya: ok first triage: 1) throttle new streaming traffic, 2) route new sessions to fallback pool (proxy-v2.13.x) 3) bump proxy read timeout while we investigate

samir: doing 1 & 2 now. kicking traffic to fallback with rollout override. applying: `traffic-route set --pool streaming-fallback --pct 100`

ops_jamie: applied. telemetry shows p99 start dropping after ~30s of switch. :thumbsup:

ingrid: increasing `proxy_read_timeout` from 30s -> 60s for the effected gateway to avoid premature connection closes (temporary).

samir: update: after routing to fallback p99 fell to ~900ms within 2m, p95 back to ~160ms. customer reports still seeing occasional 5-10s gaps but much improved

maya: can you paste the proxy error histogram? want to see tail shape.

samir: snippet from logs/metrics: 
```
stream_proxy.chunk_interval_ms P50=60 P95=720 P99=3200
conn.reset.rate 0.2% -> 1.3% (15:03-15:15)
```

kt: that P99 tail at 3200ms lines up with the alert. interesting that chunk_interval P95 is big — suggests flush not happening until threshold hit

ops_jamie: hypothesis: the new buffer/flush threshold change delays small-chunk flushes; slow consumer + buffering = head-of-line stalls. proxy then times out or resets connection when buffers hit high-water

ingrid: also seeing memory pressure on a couple proxy instances: ephemeral spikes in write buffer size.

maya: mitigation checklist for handoff: 
- keep fallback routing in place until fix validated
- keep proxy_read_timeout=60s for 30m then revert if stable
- scale additional proxy instances to relieve slow-consumer queueing
- collect tcpdump for one impacted connection and save to /tmp/stream-dumps/<id>.pcap

samir: I've scaled 3 extra proxies in prod-us-east and kicked collector for pcap on acct-42.

kt: customer impact: initial window 15:03-15:22 UTC, ~7 customers with active streaming sessions impacted, 3 customers saw degraded UX (long gap >10s), 0 data loss, 2 experienced reconnects. CC: cs-team

maya: good summary. leaving this with maya for next on-call. ping me if escalates.

maya: taking over. current state: fallback routing at 100%, proxies scaled + read timeout increased, p99 trending ~900ms. I’ll keep monitoring until stabilizes for 30m. handing off to night oncall after that if stable.

samir: followups (quick): 
- revert proxy-v2.14.7 -> roll back the flush threshold change (PR #4872)
- add instrumentation for buffered_bytes and flush_delay per connection
- add automated alert for proxy.buffered_bytes.p99 > threshold
- run canary of fixed proxy on staging with slow-consumer tests

maya: noted. I’ll create the incident ticket and link dashboards. Incident created: https://redwood.incidents/2620001234 (placeholder)

ops_jamie: note for postmortem: reproduce with `wrk` + slow consumer client that reads in 1kb chunks every 200ms to emulate mobile clients

ingrid: I’ll attach a sampling of tcpdumps and memory profiles to the ticket.

kt: any immediate customer comms? support should send an explainer and ETA for full resolution (CS draft ready)

maya: assigning action items: @samir rollback PR, @ingrid capture artifacts, @ops_jamie add canary test, @kt coordinate CS. I’ll draft postmortem timeline tomorrow.

samir: rolling back PR now. command: `deploy proxy --image proxy:v2.13.9 --selector region=us-east`

incident-bot: update — rollback started by samir at 15:32 UTC (job 8821).

samir: rollback complete. monitoring shows p99 down to ~420ms after 3m, p95 stable. reconnects stopped.

maya: thanks team. leaving monitoring in my name. if anything flares up escalate to eng-sre. closing on-call for now but keeping the incident thread open for postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:

ingrid: tagging artifacts in the ticket. will follow up with heap + tcpdump links.

kt: assigning CS message to triage; will send proactive notes to 3 impacted customers within 30m.

samir: final note: root cause likely proxy flush threshold change interacting with slow consumers. fix plan: roll back and add safer default + canary; postmortem will include latency graphs and test cases.

maya: last message before handoff: maintain fallback route until 16:10 UTC. will update when I remove it.

incident-bot: acknowledged handoff to maya (oncall) — next check-in scheduled at 15:55 UTC.
